diagnosis_explanation: Your brain had trouble sending and receiving messages. This is called aphasia. It can affect how you speak and understand others. It can also affect how you read and write.
medication_rationale:
G-tube:
This tube is a feeding tube that goes into your stomach. It is still in place in case you need it later. You do not need to use it now. Your doctor will tell you if it is time to remove it.
recovery_trajectory:
**Week 1:**
- You may feel confused and have trouble finding words. This is normal.
- Try to rest often.
- Focus on simple communication, like pointing or gestures.
- Do not eat or drink anything. This is called NPO.
- If you try to speak, do not get upset if words do not come out.
- Your goal this week is to use gestures to ask for what you need.
- Call your doctor if you get a fever or feel more confused.

**Week 2:**
- You might still find it hard to understand or express yourself.
- Rest is still important to help your brain heal.
- Keep following the NPO diet.
- Try to listen closely when others speak to you.
- Your goal this week is to communicate one need non-verbally.
- Call your doctor if you have a sudden increase in confusion.

**Week 3:**
- Some days may feel a little easier for speaking and understanding.
- Continue to rest when you feel tired.
- You must still follow the NPO diet.
- Practice saying simple sounds or words.
- Your goal this week is to point to objects when asked.
- Call your doctor if you have any trouble breathing.

**Week 4:**
- You may start to notice small improvements in understanding.
- Keep up with your rest and relaxation.
- Continue to follow the NPO diet.
- Try to repeat simple words you hear.
- Your goal this week is to nod or shake your head for yes or no.
- Call your doctor if you have a severe headache.

**When to expect improvement:**
- Improvement from aphasia can be slow. Be patient with yourself.
- Keep attending speech therapy sessions.
- Continue to rest and avoid overexertion.
- Small steps in communication will add up over time.
- Do not get discouraged by setbacks.
